title: HyperX Cloud Stinger 2 Core: A Light, Simple Gaming Headset on a Budget
summary: The HyperX Cloud Stinger 2 Core is HyperX's entry wired gaming headset: 40 mm drivers, a swivel-to-mute mic, on-ear volume control and a 3.5 mm jack that works with PC and consoles. Here's what HyperX lists, where sources differ and who it suits.
description:
## Who is it for?

- New PC and console gamers on a budget.
- Students who game and attend online classes.
- Long sessions where light weight matters.

## Why consider it?

- Light, closed-back over-ear design.
- Swivel-to-mute noise-cancelling mic.
- 3.5 mm jack plus PC splitter.

sections.title: What is the Cloud Stinger 2 Core?
sections.content: HyperX (owned by HP) positions the Cloud Stinger 2 Core as its entry wired headset: good sound, comfort and the basics done well. There are PC, PlayStation and Xbox editions; this review covers the PC version (683L9AA), which HyperX's US store lists at US$29.99.

sections.title: Comfort and build
sections.content: HyperX lists the weight at about 272–275 g depending on the page — light for an over-ear headset. Fabric-covered foam cushions stay cooler than leatherette but isolate a bit less. The frame is plastic with slider adjustment, and there is no RGB.

sections.title: Sound
sections.content: HyperX specifies 40 mm neodymium drivers, a 10 Hz–25 kHz response, 32.5 Ω impedance and 95 dBSPL/mW sensitivity. Expect punchy effects and clear enough footsteps for mainstream games. HyperX's spec page lists DTS Headphone:X spatial audio for PC; availability of the activation can vary by edition and region, so check before buying if it matters.

sections.title: Microphone and controls
sections.content: The bi-directional noise-cancelling electret mic sits on a flexible boom and mutes when you swivel it up — no need to check software. Volume is on the ear cup. The mic is not detachable, so it's not ideal as an outdoor headphone.

sections.title: Compatibility
sections.content: The 4-pole 3.5 mm jack works with PC, PS5/PS4 and Xbox controllers with a 3.5 mm port, Nintendo Switch and phones with a headphone jack; a splitter is included for PCs with separate mic and headphone ports. USB-C-only phones need an adapter.

sections.title: Who should buy it — and who shouldn't
sections.content: Buy it if you want a light, reliable first gaming headset with a decent mic. Skip it if you want wireless, RGB, a metal frame (Cloud II / Cloud III) or a detachable mic.

sections.title: Sources for this review
sections.content: Zero Technology has not used this headset in person. This is a research roundup based on HyperX's product page and HyperX Support Center specifications, checked November 2026. Where HyperX's own pages differ (weight, cable), we say so. Images are official HyperX photos.

pros: Light (about 272–275 g) and comfortable for long sessions.
Swivel-to-mute mic is fast and unambiguous.
3.5 mm jack works with PC, consoles and phones; PC splitter included.
Major gaming brand with a 2-year limited warranty.
cons: Wired only — no wireless or USB.
Fabric cushions isolate less than leatherette.

faq.question: Does it work with PS5, Xbox and phones?
faq.answer: Yes, via the 3.5 mm jack on controllers and phones that have one. USB-C-only phones need an adapter. HyperX also sells dedicated PlayStation and Xbox editions.

faq.question: Does it have surround sound?
faq.answer: There's no hardware surround. HyperX's spec page lists DTS Headphone:X spatial audio for PC.

faq.question: Is the mic detachable?
faq.answer: No, but it swivels up to mute and the boom is flexible.

faq.question: How heavy is it?
faq.answer: HyperX lists about 272–275 g depending on the page.

faq.question: Cloud Stinger 2 Core vs Cloud Stinger 2?
faq.answer: The Core is the stripped-back, cheaper model; the Cloud Stinger 2 adds extras. Compare current prices before choosing.

faq.question: What warranty does it have?
faq.answer: HyperX lists a 2-year limited warranty; check terms for your country.

seo_description: HyperX Cloud Stinger 2 Core: 40 mm drivers, about 272 g, swivel-to-mute mic, 3.5 mm for PC, PS5 and Xbox. Sourced specs, pros and cons, and alternatives.
verdict_summary: A light, comfortable entry headset with a handy swivel-to-mute mic and broad compatibility. No wireless, RGB or metal frame, but it does the basics well.

bestFor: First gaming headset on a budget
PC and console players using 3.5 mm
notFor: Anyone who wants a detachable mic for outdoor use
Buyers who want a metal frame or RGB

alternatives.note: Sturdier metal frame and USB sound card, at a higher price.
